# DOCX Render and Accessibility Verification

**Verification date:** July 20, 2026

**Scope:** Final Bible v2.8 and Roadmap v2.7 binaries generated by this package

## Exact artifacts

| Artifact | SHA-256 | Word PDF pages | PDF bytes |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Bible v2.8 | `47F9771C29A3FAEA18858865F402DF0E342840DAD80ECF4650B8ABCC537DE963` | 54 | 2,371,580 |
| Roadmap v2.7 | `899F0054483E886F79AACB4115AE0E160ACC44FA3BFFE5EEA2882A5C70EE6A83` | 61 | 1,171,939 |

Microsoft Word for Microsoft 365 opened each final DOCX read-only and exported
the PDF. Poppler reported the page counts and rasterized the PDF. The PDF is
temporary verification evidence; the controlled artifact is the DOCX whose
hash appears above.

## Latest-build visual gate

All pages of the final build were covered, including the Bible cleanup that
removed the earlier orphan terminal page:

- The earlier inspected 72-dpi Bible pages 1–52 were compared pixel-for-pixel
  with a new 72-dpi raster of the final 54-page PDF: 52 of 52 were identical.
- Final Bible pages 53–54 were separately inspected at higher resolution after
  cleanup. Appendix O and its complete chooser/requirements content fit without
  clipping or an orphan page.
- The earlier inspected 72-dpi Roadmap pages 1–61 were compared pixel-for-pixel
  with a new raster of the final 61-page PDF: 61 of 61 were identical.
- A separate 90-dpi full-page scan covered all final pages. Bible ink coverage
  ranged from 0.0369 to 0.3733; Roadmap coverage ranged from 0.0113 to 0.2605.
  It found no blank-page flags and no raster content reaching the crop edge.

The visual review covered cover/authority bands, TOC pages, portrait and
landscape sections, tables, diagrams, headers/footers, appendix transitions,
and final pages. No clipped text, table overflow, unexpected blank page,
overlap, missing glyph, broken image, or displaced header/footer was observed.

## Structure results

| Check | Bible v2.8 | Roadmap v2.7 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Heading 1 / 2 / 3 | 39 / 127 / 1 | 35 / 191 / 7 |
| Sections | 1 | 5 |
| Inline images | 10 | 1 |
| Tables | 92 | 119 |
| Marked semantic header rows | 25 | 46 |
| `PAGEREF` / `PAGE` fields | 144 / 1 | 208 / 1 |

The generator marked field starts dirty so Word can refresh the TOC and other
cached references. The field architecture remains intact. The Bible's ten
images and Roadmap's one image have alternative descriptions; three stale
Bible descriptions were corrected through exact fail-closed anchors.

## Accessibility audit

| Severity | Bible v2.8 | Roadmap v2.7 |
|---|---:|---:|
| High | 0 | 0 |
| Medium | 67 | 73 |
| Low | 0 | 0 |

Every medium result is `table_no_header_row`. Independent inspection found the
remaining unmarked structures to be inherited callouts, cards, process strips,
status bands, signature/form regions, and other visual layout tables rather
than semantic data tables. The new real data tables use marked header rows.
Blanket `first_row` repair was rejected because announcing layout content as
column headers would make the document less semantically accurate.

The audit found no high- or low-severity issue, missing image alternative text,
heading-level skip, or hyperlink problem. Style lint still reports inherited
direct formatting and TOC display-line false positives; exact counts and the
rationale for deferring global normalization are in the two template
distillation records.

## Verification boundary

This is a completed structural, accessibility, and rendered-layout audit of the
controlled artifacts. It is not an unconditional certification of every Word
reader's behavior or a claim that inherited layout tables satisfy an ideal
future document design system. Those reviewed warnings remain documented debt,
not hidden failures and not a reason to apply semantically incorrect headers.
